result.summary:
The audit's BLOCKING call is correct and survives: "Both sit at the same table." is an added claim in no WAS line, it fails 42a on its own test, and it must be cut before anything lands. Its mechanical sweep is also correct — I re-ran it over the delivered text with the WAS lines stripped and got zero hits for em dash, exclamation, semicolon, contraction, first person, will/shall, bare priest/mayor/singular elder, and every struck archaism including "drinking house", "pedlar" and "granary"; the only digit hits are metadata lines, not prose.

But the audit is INCOMPLETE in the one way that matters to the freeze: IT LEFT A CHANGED LINE UNEXAMINED. The file marks seven CHANGED faces at lines 12, 24, 31, 41, 44, 47 and 54. The return analyses six. Variant 3 face 6 [muster] — line 54, "The muster's account is that what reaches it first is the shouting, and that the shouting is enough to go on." re-cut to "The muster reckons what reaches it first is the shouting, and the shouting is enough to go on." — is named nowhere in the return, not in the findings, not in the untouched list, not in leastSure. An unexamined changed line is an unrefuted line, and it carries a real attribution defect (finding 1 below). The audit's own facesChanged count of 7 is right; its coverage is 6.

THE MOVED CLAIM IT PASSED OVER IS THE ONE IT AFFIRMATIVELY CLEARED. At variant 1 face 4 the audit records "No defect ... The claim is identical" and calls it "the model the other five untouched 42d failures should have been cut to". The claim is not identical. "the same words go over the house" names no agent; "they speak the same words over the house" makes the ground-keepers the officiants. A game master reading the new line places them at the graveside performing the rite — a fact the old line did not license, and one the standing refutation never tested. This matters twice over, because the audit flagged exactly this class as a moved claim one finding earlier at variant 3 face 2 ("what is given here" to "what they give here") and then blessed it here. Its leastSure #3 asks for the principled line between these; here it is, and it settles all four pronoun insertions: inserting the speaker as the PATIENT of an act the settlement's people still perform keeps the subject, the act and the habitual frame, so V2F1 "lends him a thing" is lawful 42d; REPLACING a generic or agentless SUBJECT with the speaker shrinks the claim, so V3F1 "a visitor here learns" to "he learns", V3F2, and V1F4 are all narrowings that must be collected for re-refutation. The audit collected two of the three and cleared the third.

ITS REMEDIES ARE LESS SAFE THAN ITS DIAGNOSES. The shape finding is right that 20 of 20 faces are role-says-a-fact and right that the freeze forecloses most alternatives, but its three "free conversions" each strip the reporting verb and turn a source's self-report into an engine-asserted fact; the brief licenses the speakerless shape only "where the engine itself holds it", which is the clause the finding does not quote. Its V2F4 fix keeps "the men who take the work" — the very class its own finding says may be invented and off-card. And across the twelve untouched lines, several proposed fixes are themselves 42b sharpenings that pick a reading (the variant 1 spine's "a running account of which house owes which", variant 2 face 3's "they let a stranger in on what is in his pack"), yet only one of them, V2F6, carries the re-refute caveat. Every one of those needs the caveat or none do.

Two smaller corrections. The pair-1 claim is overstated: the narrowed elders line still collides head on with the tavern half over the elders' own giving, because the tavern half covers all giving — the disagreement narrows, it does not stop. And the headline arithmetic does not close: 23 lines minus 12 untouched failures leaves 11, and the audit's own findings fail three more changed lines (V3F3, V3F2, V2F4) with a fourth never assessed, which gives 8 passing, not the 10 reported. The direction of the gain is real; the number should not be quoted.

The second "that" was dropped, which lets the second clause escape the attribution: "The muster reckons X, and the shouting is enough to go on" can be parsed as a claim the muster makes or as the narrator's own assertion coordinated with the whole main clause. Under the WAS line a game master knows only that the muster THINKS shouting is enough, and can play the muster as complacent and wrong; under one available reading of the NOW line the shouting really is enough, which is an engine-held fact about the settlement's readiness and not a muster opinion. That is a moved claim on the reading, and a 42b breach in any case, because two readings now fit the sentence. Separately "The muster's account is that" became "The muster reckons", which downgrades a report the muster has given into an opinion it holds; on a pool whose machinery turns on witnesses and what is on the record, those are different facts. Restoring the parallel "that" fixes both the ambiguity and the escape while keeping the shorter verb the implementer wanted.

The NOW line names the ground-keepers as the ones who speak, which is a fact about who performs the rite that the old line did not carry and the standing refutation never tested. A game master reading the new line now places the keepers at the graveside officiating; under the old line a local priest could have spoken and the line would still be true. This is the identical class of change the audit itself calls a moved claim one finding earlier at variant 3 face 2, where a generic subject was replaced by the speakers, and the two cannot be decided differently. The pool's own state makes the reading plausible rather than safe: variant 2 face 2 has the keepers arranging a burying and variant 3 face 4 has them observing who attends, so the register card may well carry it — which is the reason to re-refute it, not to clear it. The fix is to collect it with the other sharpenings; if the card will not grant the keepers the speaking, the agentless WAS construction must come back with the 42d stake taken from somewhere else.

If the card does not make the ground-keepers the ones who speak over a house, restore: Those who keep the ground say the same words go over the house that gives everything and the house that gives nothing.

Its proposed fix, "At the tavern the men who take the work say one house gives the word and another house does the work", keeps "the men who take the work" — the class the same finding says is not what the [tavern] source already IS on its card, and 42d requires the stake be drawn from the card and never invented. There is a further consequence the finding does not draw: the WAS face was the tavern crowd reporting on two houses from outside, and the NOW face is one of those houses' own men reporting their own grievance, which converts neutral town talk into interested testimony and changes how a game master weighs it. overturnedFindings.faceOrSpine: SHAPE_MONOTONY — the three proposed "free conversions" (V1F4, V1F6, V3F5)
overturnedFindings.why: The diagnosis survives and should go to the chair: all 20 faces are role-says-a-fact, and the freeze's "no speaker deleted, no attribution dropped" really does foreclose most of the lawful alternatives. The remedy does not survive. The brief licenses the speakerless shape in one clause the finding does not quote: "the bare fact with no speaker where the engine itself holds it." Each proposed conversion strips the reporting verb from a line whose content is a source's claim, and so asserts as engine-held fact what was only alleged. V1F6 is the clearest: "Whoever holds the way through says they wave a cart on as soon as they know what it carries" is a gatekeeper's self-report about his own diligence, which is exactly the class this programme treats as concealable by a compromised role, and "Whoever holds the way through waves a cart on ..." makes it true. Calling that "drops no attribution at all" is wrong: the source tag survives in metadata, but in the delivered prose nobody is speaking any more. The shape conversion is only free where the engine holds the fact, and none of the three were checked against that.

This one should be struck from the remainder list rather than cut. The audit calls "and nobody there says why" a trailing clause that adds no fact and is the writer pointing at significance. It adds a fact: that the reason goes unspoken, which a game master can act on directly the moment a player asks anyone at the burying why that house came early. Apply 42a's own test and the clause earns its place, because deleting it loses that fact. The owner's worked lines sanction precisely this construction — "the gatekeeper locks the gate at night and opens it for anyone he knows" is a coordinate clause carrying a second fact, not an explanation of the first. The proposed fix would delete a usable fact from a line the implementer never touched, which is a regression introduced by the audit rather than a defect found by it.

missedFindings.was: Those who sell at the market say a household with somebody ill in it comes late and buys small, and that the stalls know a sick house sooner than the parish.

missedFindings.why: The auditor blessed this split as surviving 42a and never checked the frame. The second fact was inside 'say ... and that ...' — a stallholder's claim. It is now a full stop away from its verb and fully self-standing, so it reads as the narrator's own assertion. A game master reading the new line believes the stalls DO know before the parish; the old line licensed only that the market people say so. Under ruling 40 a bare sentence is an engine fact, so the cut promoted a stallholder's brag to the engine's own voice. That is both a dropped attribution (the freeze: NO ATTRIBUTION DROPPED) and a moved claim. The auditor flagged exactly this on the V2 SPINE and rated it a NOTE because a spine is unsourced — the same defect on a sourced [market] face got no entry at all. The distinction that proves it: the two HEAD lines that are already two sentences (V1 F4 'The tending has neither' and V2 F5 'Nobody makes that good') are anaphorically bound and cannot be read as narration; this new sentence has no back-reference and can.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Revert the split and keep the 'that' deletion, which is the minimal freeze-safe repair: 'Those who sell at the market say a household with somebody ill in it comes late and buys small, and the stalls know a sick house sooner than the parish.' If the split is wanted for rhythm, re-hook the second sentence: '... and buys small. The stalls know a sick house sooner than the parish does, they say.' — the trailing attribution the pool already uses at V1 F3 and V3 F2.

missedFindings.was: A clerk in the hall says the store is the town's to keep and not the town's to open.
missedFindings.now: A clerk in the hall says the store the hall keeps is the town's, and not the town's to open.
missedFindings.why: The auditor recorded this only as a possible change-of-doer and handed the disposition to the chair with no entry on the 42b collection list. That is the miss, because it lands unrefuted on the KEEP branch. 'The store is the town's to keep' carries two readings — the town owns it and is its custodian, or it is within the town's right to keep though not to open. The new line commits to one: the HALL is the custodian and the TOWN is the owner, two separate facts where the old line had one undifferentiated one. By the brief's own words a sharpened line is 'NOT covered by the old refutation and MUST be collected separately'. A NOTE saying 'revert or keep, chair's call' with no collection row means that if the chair keeps it — which the auditor half-endorses as a 42d win — the face ships with no refutation behind it.
missedFindings.proposedFix: No text change needed. Put this face on the 42b list that goes to the refuter, with the reading stated: the hall is the store's keeper and the town its owner. If the chair instead reads the freeze strictly and reverts to the HEAD line, the collection row can be struck.

missedFindings.now: ... and no drinker there has ever bothered.
missedFindings.why: The auditor caught the scope narrowing (nobody in the town becomes nobody in that room) and then wrote that 'the plainer has ever bothered' is 'good and should be kept'. It is not. Two facts ride in on it that the old line did not carry. 'Bothered' imputes a motive — indifference, a thing not worth the walk — where 'does' stated only that they do not; 42d says the stake must come from what the source already is, 'never an invented motive'. And 'has ever' converts a present habitual into a perfect covering all past time, which is the same habitual-to-tense move the auditor called BLOCKING at V2 F7, running the other way. A game master reading the new line believes the locals are incurious about their own grain store; the old line licensed only that they do not walk up to it.
missedFindings.proposedFix: At the tavern they say strangers walk up to look at the store, and nobody in the town does. (Repairs the scope the auditor found and drops the imported motive and tense in the same edit.)

I applied the 42a delete test to each: 'nobody at the table knows the hand', 'nobody has ordered it to', 'the purse has no line in it for a parish', 'the stalls know a sick house sooner than the parish', 'whoever tends a sick house here comes out of the church', 'nobody born here asks for the house', 'nobody here does' — every one carries a fact the first clause does not, so every one earns its place and ruling 42 was never engaged by any of them. The edits are a small plainness gain, not the fix the auditor credits. This matters to the verdict, not just the prose: seven of the fifteen changed faces are cosmetic, so the auditor's 13-of-25 to 20-of-25 pass count has no support I can reconstruct, and the cut did materially less than the audit says it did.

missedFindings.faceOrSpine: FACES 2, 4, 5, 7 [market, register, guild, gate] and V3 FACE 5 [guild]
missedFindings.was: say / says (16 across the pool at HEAD)
missedFindings.now: reckon (V1 F2) · has it that (V1 F4) · hold that (V1 F5) · reports that (V1 F7) · reckons (V3 F5)
missedFindings.why: The auditor filed all five under SHAPE_MONOTONY as a style tic and made the epistemic argument for only one of them — that 'has it that' 'downgrades the priest from a man stating a fact to a source of hearsay, which weakens the attribution the freeze protects'. That argument is correct and it applies to four more. 'Reckon' and 'reckons' convert an asserted fact into an estimate the speaker holds; 'hold that' converts it into a position; 'has it that' into hearsay. What a game master can rely on changes: at HEAD the market people STATE that the store takes no part in the price of the loaf, and after the cut they merely SUPPOSE it. Under the freeze that is the fact's standing moving, not its wording, and it lifts these five from a style note to a freeze-adjacent breach on five of fifteen changed faces. The auditor's own remedy already covers it, which is why I file this as a re-rating rather than a separate repair.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Restore plain 'says' on all five, as the auditor proposed for a different reason. Note also that 'reckon' is not itself a plain modern word under 42c — it is regional register — so the swap fails the rule it was presumably reaching for.

overturnedFindings.faceOrSpine: VARIANT 1 FACE 8 [garrison] — the RULING_42b_STILL_VAGUE finding ('nobody has ordered it to' has two readings)
overturnedFindings.why: The pronoun collision does not survive. The auditor says the nearest antecedent for 'it' is 'the store', so two readings fit and by 42b the line makes no claim. Only one reading is semantically available: a store cannot be ordered to stand in front of anything, and the garrison is a collective singular that takes 'it' in exactly this construction ('the garrison ... it') — the sentence's own subject. A reader does not entertain the store-reading long enough to call it a reading. 42b's test is 'if two readings FIT the sentence', not if two nouns precede the pronoun. The auditor put this in their own leastSure list, and the doubt was the right instinct. What survives untouched is the other half of their pair: the SHARPENING_42b entry on the same face is correct, the narrowing from 'nobody's order' at large to 'no order given to the garrison' is real, and that face must go to the refuter. The elided infinitive after 'to' is a mild infelicity worth the copy edit, not a 42b breach, and the proposed repair ('nobody has ordered the garrison to stand there') is fine to take on those grounds alone.

result.summary: The audit is sound where it looked and missed the thing it was most pointed at. I re-ran the mechanical sweep myself and it is CONFIRMED clean on every bar — no em dash, semicolon, exclamation, digit in prose, will/shall, first person, bare role or brace, and all five apostrophes are possessives; granary survives only in the pool's title line and factor only in two WAS lines, so the 42c cure did land in both places. Both BLOCKING calls survive independent checking: V2 F7 really does convert a habitual into a one-off past event, and V3 F1's 'is sent him instead' really does swap an unnamed person for the speaking priest while widening 'the house' to 'a house at all'. One finding is overturned: the 42b pronoun collision at V1 F8 does not stand, because only one antecedent for 'it' is semantically available; the sharpening the auditor filed on the same face is correct and stays. The material miss is a dropped attribution on a sourced face — V2 FACE 4 [market], where the cut split a sentence and left the second fact self-standing, turning a stallholder's claim into the engine's own assertion. The auditor caught exactly this pattern on the V2 SPINE, rated it a NOTE because a spine is unsourced, and then blessed the identical split on a sourced face as 'surviving the 42a test'. The test it needed was not 42a but the frame: the two lines that were already two sentences at HEAD both have anaphorically bound second sentences ('neither', 'that good') that cannot be read as narration, and this new one has no back-reference at all. Three further misses: V1 F1 is an undeclared 42b sharpening that the auditor filed as a chair question with no collection row, so on the keep branch it ships unrefuted; V3 F3's 'has ever bothered', which the auditor called good and worth keeping, imports a motive (indifference) and a perfect tense the old line did not carry; and the five attribution-verb swaps change the claim's standing from asserted to believed, an argument the auditor made for 'has it that' alone and did not carry to the other four. Finally the credit is inflated. There were seven 'and that' edits, not six, and I applied the 42a delete test to all seven — every surviving clause carries a fact, so ruling 42 was never engaged by any of them and those edits are cosmetic. The 13-of-25 to 20-of-25 pass count is not reconstructible on that basis and should be re-derived before the chair reads it. Disposition unchanged in kind but not in weight: still LANDABLE_AFTER_FIXES, now with three BLOCKING repairs rather than two, and with V1 F1, V1 F8 and V3 F3 all needing collection for the refuter.
